questions.question: There are 15 students in a class. Their average weight is 40 kg. When one student leaves the class, the average weight is 39.5 kg. What is the weight of the student who left the class (where kg means kilogram)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

There are 15 students in a class.

Their average weight is 40 kg.

When one student leaves the class, the average weight is 39.5 kg.

**Calculation:**

The total weight of 15 students is 15 × 40 = 600 kg

The total weight of 14 students is 14 × 39.5 = 553 kg

The weight of new students is 600 - 553 = 47 kg

**∴ The correct option is** 1

questions.question: Rekha alone can complete a work in 16 days, and Bina alone can complete the same work in 12 days. Starting with Rekha, they work on alternate days. The total work will be completed in:
questions.solution:
Given: 

Rekha alone can complete a work in 16 days, and Bina alone can complete the same work in 12 days.

Starting with Rekha, they work on alternate days.

Concept used:

Efficiency = (Total work / Total time taken)

Efficiency = work done in a single day 

Calculation:

Let the total work is the 48 units (LCM of 16 and 12)

The efficiency of Rekha is 48 / 16 = 3 units

The efficiency of Bina is 48 / 12 = 4 units

In 2 days they do 3 + 4 = 7 units

They do 42 units of work in 6 × 2 = 12 days

Then Rekha does 3 units in 1 day 

Then Bina does 3 units in 3/4 day 

Total number of days will be 12 + 1 + 3/4 = 13(3)/(4) days

∴ The correct option is 4

Single discount equivalent to two successive discounts of a % and b %

Here, a = 17 % , and b = 9 %

⇒ (26 - 1.53) %

⇒ 24.47%

questions.question: The area of the sector of a circle of radius 28 cm is 112 cm². Find the length of the corresponding arc of the sector.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of Sector = (1/2) × Radius × Arc length

112 = (1/2) × 28 × l

112 = 14 × l

l = 112 / 14 = 8 cm

**∴ The correct option is B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius (r) = 28 cm

Area of sector (A) = 112 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Area of sector = (Arc length × Radius) / 2

 

 r = 28 cm
 Area = 112 cm²
 Arc length (l) = ?
 Sector of a Circle

**Calculations:**

⇒ 112 = (l × 28) / 2

⇒ 112 = l × 14

⇒ l = 112 / 14

⇒ l = 8 cm

**∴ The correct option is B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arc Length Formula

The length of an arc (l) with central angle θ is given by l = (θ/360) × 2πr.

Sector Area Formula

The area of a sector (A) with central angle θ is given by A = (θ/360) × πr².

Perimeter of a Sector

The total perimeter of a sector is the sum of the arc length and the two radii: P = l + 2r.

Relationship between Area and Arc Length

Area of sector = (1/2) × r × l, where r is the radius and l is the arc length.</p

questions.question: John got 20% marks in an examination and failed by 10 marks. In the same examination, Jack got 35% marks which were 20 more than the minimum passing marks. Find the percentage of minimum marks required to pass.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in Percentage = 35% − 20% = 15%

Difference in Marks = 20 − (−10) = 30 marks

15% → 30 marks ∴ 1% → 2 marks

John needs 10 more marks to pass → 10 ÷ 2 = 5% extra

Passing Percentage = 20% + 5% = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

John: 20% marks, Failed by 10 marks.

Jack: 35% marks, 20 marks more than pass.

**Formula Used:**

Passing Marks = (Total Marks × Pass %) / 100

 
• 
 
 
 20% (John)
 
 
 Pass %
 
 
 35% (Jack)
 
 

 +10 marks
 
 

 −20 marks
 
 Total Gap = 30 Marks = 15%

Let the total marks be x.

⇒ Passing marks = (20/100) × x + 10

⇒ Passing marks = (35/100) × x − 20

⇒ 0.20x + 10 = 0.35x − 20

⇒ 10 + 20 = 0.35x − 0.20x

⇒ 30 = 0.15x

⇒ x = 30 / 0.15

⇒ x = 200 marks

⇒ Passing marks = (20/100) × 200 + 10 = 40 + 10 = 50 marks

⇒ Passing percentage = (50 / 200) × 100

⇒ Passing percentage = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

To find the percentage change, use the formula: % Change = (Difference / Original Value) × 100.

Total Marks Calculation

Total Marks = (Sum of marks deficiency and excess) / (Difference in percentage) × 100.

Passing Marks Relation

Passing Marks = Passed Marks − Excess Marks OR Failed Marks + Marks Deficiency.</p

questions.question: The fourth proportional of the numbers 8, 12 and 14 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of the first two numbers is 8 : 12 = 2 : 3.

For them to be in proportion, the third and fourth numbers must share the exact same ratio.

Let the fourth proportional be x, so 14 : x = 2 : 3.

x = (14 × 3) ÷ 2 = 21.

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The given numbers are 8, 12, and 14.

**Formula Used:**

If four numbers a, b, c, and d are in proportion, then a : b :: c : d.

In any proportion, the Product of Extremes equals the Product of Means (a × d = b × c).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/85d7965c2ff11b2085b36f9b6a5618185f231a6831507c737882ffb7ae966fd1.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the fourth proportional be x.

⇒ 8 : 12 :: 14 : x

⇒ 8 ÷ 12 = 14 ÷ x

⇒ 8 × x = 12 × 14

⇒ 8x = 168

⇒ x = 168 ÷ 8

⇒ x = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Third Proportional

If a and b are two numbers, their third proportional c satisfies a : b = b : c, which gives the formula c = b² ÷ a.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between any two given numbers a and b is calculated using the formula √(a × b).

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

If four numbers are in proportion such that a : b = c : d, then by this rule, (a + b) ÷ (a − b) = (c + d) ÷ (c − d).

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks his goods in such a way that after allowing a discount of 22% he gains 20%. If the cost price of the article is ₹650, then its marked price is:
questions.solution:
Given:

A shopkeeper marks his goods in such a way that after allowing a discount of 22% he gains 20%. If the cost price of the article is ₹650

Formula used:

If a shopkeeper wants a profit of R% after allowing a discount of r%

Then cost price = Market price × (100-r)/(100+R)

Calculation:

As per the question,

650 = marked price × (100 - 22) / (100 + 20)

⇒ marked price = 650 × 120 / 78

⇒ Rs 1000

So the **marked **price of the article is Rs 1000
